correctness.rationale: Legendre's formula gives (p-1)W_p(n)=2S_p(n)-(n-1)s_p(n). Splitting at p^L gives the displayed exact difference, with all terms except (a+1)s_p(t) divisible by p^L after multiplication by p-1. The alternate carry formula can be checked by counting, for each m=p^h, those j for which j mod m exceeds n mod m in each complete block; it gives W_p(n) divisible by p^j whenever n+1 is. On aligned p^i-blocks the digit-sum character bound is |1+zeta+...+zeta^(p-1)|^i. Choosing a common upper bound strictly between max(1,max_zeta |1+...+zeta^(p-1)|) and p, then summing over the at most p-1 blocks per scale in a prefix, gives a power saving for arbitrary cutoffs. For j<k, the linear coefficient in the compressed congruence has exact valuation j, so the conditional law is uniform on p^j multiples; j>=k forces zero. Each j<k contributes (p-1)/p^(k+1) per permissible residue, and the last stratum adds p^(-k) at zero. The histogram is the generating-function count of tail digit sums, including r=k; one free digit already gives exact uniformity modulo p. For L>=1, setting a=0 gives a remainder coefficient congruent to -(L+1) at t=1 and to -L at t=p+1, so some remainder has valuation exactly L. At L=0 the witness a=0,t=1 works for every k>=1 since W_p(1)=0 and (p-1)^(-1) is a unit. Independent Legendre-valuation enumeration supplied 1,406 bounded checks at p=2,3,5 (blocks up to 2,000 indices); replay: /workspace/branches/3e039027-151e-40e3-bbc6-20471bee4a29/replay.py and replay-output.txt in that directory. The finite replay does not establish the natural density or the uniform quantifiers.

value.rationale: The valuation of a full Pascal row product is a natural aggregate rather than a selected binomial coefficient. Its nonuniform law is explained by the valuation strata of n+1, and the sharp split depth gives an exact finite counting procedure at arbitrary output precision. These give distinct usable information on the whole sequence beyond the known term formula.
